summary: Ten comment-endorsed discoveries spanning diagramming, embedded scripting, hardware, ambient audio, and thoughtful media.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 past front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Pele
items.source_story_title: Pele – Mermaid diagrams as themeable SVG
items.summary: Mermaid-to-SVG renderer; a static-site user preferred its layouts after switching.
items.why_included: A concrete migration report supports the recommendation beyond launch-day enthusiasm.
items.evidence: bilibali replaced Mermaid.js in a static-site build and preferred Pele's layouts despite layout differences.

evidence_sources.author: bilibali
evidence_sources.excerpt: This seemed like a perfect fit for my use case and I already swapped it in. I noticed that the layouts were not 1 to 1, but to my pleasant surprise I actually liked the ones Pele renders better than mermaidjs.

items.name: D2
items.source_story_title: Pele – Mermaid diagrams as themeable SVG

items.why_included: A named alternative with a specific first-hand reason for switching.
items.evidence: burgeonlab switched to D2Lang for easier syntax and dissatisfaction with Mermaid's AI push.

evidence_sources.author: burgeonlab
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've switched to D2Lang for its easier syntax and the fact Mermaid is hard pushing AI.

items.name: mlua
items.source_story_title: Teal – A statically-typed dialect of Lua
items.summary: Lua bindings for Rust, praised as excellent and full-featured after extensive use.
items.why_included: Strong first-hand endorsement of a practical embedded-scripting library.
items.evidence: petcat reports extensive Lua use through mlua and calls the library excellent and full-featured.

evidence_sources.author: petcat
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've used Lua extensively with Rust via the mlua library and it's excellent and full-featured.

items.name: Bambu Lab A1
items.summary: Desktop 3D printer; a used-unit owner describes a download-and-print experience.
items.why_included: An owner reports practical printing success rather than hypothetical hardware potential.
items.evidence: TacticalCoder bought a used A1 and confirms the download-and-print experience, while qualifying praise of Bambu's practices.

evidence_sources.author: TacticalCoder
evidence_sources.excerpt: I bought a cheap, used, Bambu Lab A1 printer after reading a comment here on HN a few months ago saying that it was basically now "download and print". And it's just that. Not saying Bambu's practices are great: what I'm saying is that 3D printer now work better than inkjet 2D printers ever did.

items.name: Vacuula
items.source_story_title: Custom server to revive neato bots
items.summary: Replacement server for Neato robot vacuums; Gen3 connectivity retains a nip.io dependency.
items.why_included: A repair-oriented project earns independent praise, with a concrete connectivity caveat.
items.evidence: BitBangingBytes calls the project awesome; hypfer flags the Gen3 nip.io dependency and its documentation visibility.

evidence_sources.author: BitBangingBytes
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is awesome!! I remember reverse engineering the Neato LIDAR long ago. It’s come a long way since then.

evidence_sources.author: hypfer
evidence_sources.excerpt: Generation 3 robots (after being bitten by vacuula) currently use nip.io to help connect to your server, this is a limitation of the models we haven't managed to work around cleanly yet. That permanent cloud dependency should probably be on the main readme
